design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing only: the hearing aid claim her audiologist
sent through this morning is sitting undecided and she wants it settled before she leaves the shop.
Nothing else is asked for and nothing else is hinted at. To settle it correctly the agent has to
discover, from the published rules and the records alone, that the rider is not in force at all
because rider premium has gone unpaid past its grace period; that the money standing owed is not the
figure the rider record shows, because the plan has been holding money of hers on the medical plan
bill it never split across to the rider; that part of what has been charged was never owed, a
quarterly rider premium charge having been raised from the medical plan's bill cycle a month before
the rider took effect; and that a settled eyeglass frame line marked as adjusted is still eating the
benefit year's maximum that the hearing aid needs. Each of those is a separate problem with its own
multi-factor figure, and the order they are resolved in is forced by what the rules say each figure
waits on. The difficulty is entirely in reading the policy and reconciling the ledgers: no tool has
to be guessed at, no information is missing, and the caller volunteers nothing that would shorten the
work.

SCOPE TAKEN AND SCOPE LEFT. This is the first task of the difficulty, so nothing was occupied before
it. It claims four extended policies and the four task tools they name:
osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement (settle_rider_benefit_line_e49937be),
osb_ext_adjusted_line_restatement (reverse_rider_benefit_line_9daedfb7),
osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement (pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982) and
osb_ext_precover_premium_credit (post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6). Between them they take the two
benefit-claim event subjects (osb_benefit_claim_processed and osb_benefit_claim_reversal) and two of
the three rider premium ledger subjects (osb_rider_premium_payment and osb_rider_premium_credit).
What is deliberately left for task 1 is the rider lifecycle and the third ledger subject: raising
rider premium for coverage months never billed (osb_rider_premium_charge), recording a suspension for
unpaid premium (osb_premium_suspension) and the member's own ending of the rider
(osb_rider_termination), together with the base policies osb_termination_and_cancellation and
osb_premium_suspension_and_recovery as the writes they govern. Those are a load-bearing tree of their
own -- a closing figure that depends on a suspension figure that depends on a charge -- so task 1 is
not left working around this one.

THE DRAW. scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/optional_rider_benefit_desk --task 0
prints: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/optional_rider_benefit_desk/0",
"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4, 5]}. The tree therefore carries
exactly three prerequisite problems besides the root, and the four factor counts are taken as
follows: osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement 5, osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement 6,
osb_ext_precover_premium_credit 4, osb_ext_adjusted_line_restatement 5.

THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root  osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement -- settle the submitted hearing aid line.
  edge  osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement <- osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement, kind state_gate,
        gate osb_riders.status, form state, resolved by
        pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982, owner user. Prerequisite sentence: "A benefit is not
        settled on a submitted line until the rider it is claimed under stands in force with no rider
        premium outstanding against it." Four-point test: (1) the
        ordering connective is "until", in the negated direction, and it joins this policy's own
        result -- the benefit settled on a submitted line -- to what it waits on; the affirmative
        contrapositive, "a benefit is settled on a submitted line only once the rider it is claimed
        under stands in force with no rider premium outstanding against it", carries the same result, the same waited-on state and the same scope, with no
        condition added, dropped or split; the negated form was chosen because a desk settling a
        claim tells a member what it will not do yet, which is how this line of business speaks about
        a payment it is withholding. (2) The XX side is a state the records show: the standing of
        the rider and the rider premium outstanding against it, in the words find_osb_riders
        returns, and it speaks of the record as it stands rather than of any past day, which is
        what the eligibility it gates turns on. (3) It names no tool, no policy id and no code
        token. (4) Its strength is exactly the edge's: a hard requirement ("not ... until"), no
        wider and no narrower than the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only
        pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982 can take rider_premium_balance_due to nothing and
        return status to active, since post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6 only reduces the balance,
        post_rider_premium_charge_4237e97e only raises it, suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513
        moves the rider the other way and end_rider_at_member_request_09efad65 ends it. Derivation: a
        reader sees from the sentence that a benefit waits on the rider standing in force with
        nothing outstanding; the records show premium_suspended and 219.00 USD standing; the arrears
        policy's own rule says what the money a member is asked for comes to and that paying it
        restores the rider, so the one action that answers is the member's own payment.
  edge  osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement <- osb_ext_adjusted_line_restatement, kind value_input,
        gate benefit_used, form state, resolved by reverse_rider_benefit_line_9daedfb7, owner agent.
        Prerequisite sentence: "What is left of the benefit year's maximum is not worked out before a
        reversal stands on the member's benefit history against every settled line the plan has
        marked as adjusted." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "before", negated direction; the
        affirmative contrapositive, "what is left of the benefit year's maximum is worked out only
        after a reversal stands ... adjusted", is the exact equivalent; the negated form reads as the
        business speaks of a figure it will not strike yet. (2) The XX side is a record-visible
        state: a reversal standing against the adjusted lines. (3) No tool, id or code token. (4)
        Scope exactly the edge's: every adjusted line, no wider. Exactly one write brings it about:
        only reverse_rider_benefit_line_9daedfb7 creates an osb_benefit_claim_reversal row naming a
        source line. Derivation: the sentence says the figure waits on reversals standing against
        adjusted lines; the claim history shows one line marked adjusted and no reversal at all; the
        restatement policy's own rule says it puts right the adjusted line carrying the most money by
        backing it out, so that is the action.
  edge  osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement <- osb_ext_precover_premium_credit, kind value_input, gate
        credits_counted, form state, resolved by post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6, owner agent.
        Prerequisite sentence: "The money a member is asked for is fixed only after every rider
        premium charge raised for a coverage month beginning before the day the rider took effect
        carries a credit against it." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only after",
        affirmative direction; the negated contrapositive, "the money a member is asked for is not
        fixed until every rider premium charge raised for a coverage month beginning before the day
        the rider took effect carries a credit against it", is the exact equivalent; the affirmative
        form was chosen because a figure a desk is about to quote to a member is stated as something
        it fixes once its grounds are in place, which is how a billing desk writes it. (2) The XX
        side is record-visible: charges, their coverage months, the rider effective date and whether
        a credit names them. (3) No tool, id or code token. (4) Scope exactly the edge's. Exactly one
        write brings it about: only post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6 creates an
        osb_rider_premium_credit row naming a charge. Derivation: the sentence says the figure waits
        on every pre-cover charge carrying a credit; the ledger shows the 2026-01-01 charge booked to
        coverage month 2026-01 while the rider took effect 2026-02-01, and the only credit on the
        account names the April charge; the credit policy's own rule says what is owed back on such a
        charge, so that is the action.
  Topological order: osb_ext_precover_premium_credit, osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement,
  osb_ext_adjusted_line_restatement, osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement. The parallel branches are
  shown to commute in prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness; the one order that is not free is fixed
  by the arrears policy's own prerequisite sentence. Each edge's seed evidence and deletion
  sensitivity are recorded in prerequisite_closure. The persona proof and the proof that no tool
  validates a prerequisite are recorded there too.
  At least one problem is the customer's own write: osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement is resolved by
  pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982, declared @tool(owner="user"), and the gold reaches it
  through unlock_user_discoverable_tool at action 11 and call_user_discoverable_tool at action 12.
  The in-person semantics are genuine -- it is money out of the member's own pocket, authorised by
  her on the call -- and it completes on the spot: the money is posted, the balance falls to nothing
  and the rider returns to active inside the same frozen clock, with no clearing and no batch.

THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write osb_rider_premium_credit (osb_ext_precover_premium_credit). Governing base policy:
  osb_rider_premium_billing_and_posting. Gate rider_open_for_billing, kind state, authority
  system_record, correlation osb_riders.osb_rider_id bound to the action's osb_rider_id: the rider
  stands premium_suspended, which is one of the three standings the gate allows, so it holds before
  the write. Gate payment_not_already_posted does not apply, its applies_to naming only
  osb_rider_premium_payment. No time gate on this subject.
  Write osb_rider_premium_payment (osb_ext_rider_arrears_settlement). Same governing policy. Gate
  rider_open_for_billing holds as above. Gate payment_not_already_posted, kind dedup: the account
  carries one payment, posted 2026-01-12 with remittance reference RIDG-0112-44810 and amount 199.50;
  the payment being made carries reference RIDG-2609-31775 and amount 38.30, so neither the reference
  nor the amount repeats and the gate holds. No time gate.
  Write osb_benefit_claim_reversal (osb_ext_adjusted_line_restatement). Governing policies:
  osb_claim_reversal_and_correction, osb_agg_combined_rider_maximum, osb_predetermination_and_appeal.
  Gate original_line_on_record, kind state: the line named carries claim status adjusted, which the
  gate's allowed set contains, and it is on record with its own reference. Gate
  reversal_not_already_posted, kind dedup: no osb_benefit_claim_reversal row exists on this rider at
  all, so no reversal of that line is already on record. The other two policies carry no eligibility
  for this subject and are inherited as policy scope. No time gate.
  Write osb_benefit_claim_processed (osb_ext_rider_benefit_line_settlement). Governing policies:
  osb_benefit_payment, osb_coordination_with_medical_plan, osb_predetermination_and_appeal,
  osb_agg_combined_rider_maximum, osb_frequency_limitations. Gate rider_in_force_on_service_date,
  kind state: its condition is anchored on the date of service of the line, and the aid was fitted
  on 2026-06-12, when the rider still stood in force -- the ninety days of grace on the unpaid
  April charge ran to 2026-06-30, so no suspension had arisen by then -- and the gate therefore
  holds at the opening, on the record as it stands. No gold action establishes it. Gate
  rider_in_force_for_coordination, kind state, allowed set active or waiting_period: anchored on
  the same date of service and holding at the opening for the same reason. Neither of these is
  what the member's payment answers. What the payment answers is this settlement policy's own
  prerequisite sentence, whose gate is osb_riders.status -- the rider's standing now, not its
  standing on the date of service -- and that is the one thing about this write that is false at
  the opening and true at handling time. Gate predetermination_on_record, kind authorization: the line's
  allowed amount of 2150.00 USD is above the 750.00 USD threshold the tier publishes, and rider
  service request 9a1c4e7b carries a treatment plan answered approved in part on 2026-06-04,
  inside the twelve months an approval holds good for and before the work began. Gate predetermination_answered_in_time, kind time:
  the anchor is the date the plan received the treatment plan, osb_rider_requests.created_at =
  2026-05-28; the duration is variants.predetermination_decision_days = 10 for the tier held;
  calendar days are counted from the day after that receipt date, every day of the week counting,
  an answer on the final day being in time, so the last day in time is 2026-06-07 and the plan
  answered 2026-06-04, before the work began on 2026-06-12. Positive case: an answer on 2026-06-07
  is in time because the boundary is inclusive. Negative case: an answer on 2026-06-08 is out of
  time, and the line could not rest on it. The whole temporal_basis
  is copied verbatim into solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility.
  Nothing in base is deviated from except where declared. Two clauses of osb_benefit_payment are
  superseded, both declared clause by clause in the extended policies: the out-of-network sentence,
  because this difficulty takes the out-of-network share as what is carried into the benefit
  calculation before any flat allowance or percentage rather than as a replacement for the category
  share; and the annual maximum sentence, because what is left of the maximum is worked out from the
  settled lines and the reversals rather than from the figure standing on the rider record. Base's
  parameter values are untouched and stay base-homed.

THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
  The object the call points at is one claim line: osb_benefit_claims row 04b7fd52, the hearing aid
  fitted to the right ear on 2026-09-21, allowed at 2150.00 USD, standing pended. The correlation key
  is that reference; it is the only line on the rider still awaiting a decision, so no other line on
  the same rider can be meant. The lines that enter the benefit already paid in the benefit year are
  the nine settled lines on the same rider -- eight with claim status paid and one marked adjusted --
  plus the reversal this call posts; the pended line itself is excluded by its own standing, which is
  what keeps a line from counting against the maximum before it is settled. The object the correction
  points at is osb_benefit_claims row bf62a80d, the eyeglass frame line of 2026-06-19, correlated by
  its own reference and singled out by the claim status adjusted that no other line carries; the
  reversal carries that reference in source_claim_id, so the correction is tied to its source object
  and not merely to the rider. On the premium side the object of the credit is
  osb_rider_premium_ledger row 8e2c41b7, the charge of 2026-01-01, named in the credit's
  source_premium_entry_id; the existing credit of 2026-04-08 already settles part of a different
  charge, row a2f95c60, and names it, so the two credits cannot be confused. The object of the
  payment is the oldest unpaid coverage month, row a2f95c60.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  The member profile carries the two credentials the identity check is passed on and the locating
  name; remove the Medicare identifier and the caller cannot be verified at all.
  The medical plan enrollment b81d4f27 is what the rider hangs on: its quarterly billing frequency
  decides that one rider premium charge carries three coverage months, and its coverage effective
  date of 2026-01-01 is what the month charged before cover began is counted from. Remove it and the
  credit falls from 66.50 to 24.94 USD by the first factor and to 0.00 by the third.
  The six medical plan premium ledger rows are the heart of the arrears trap: 650.00 USD paid against
  535.80 USD charged in the span from the rider effective date leaves 114.20 USD of the member's
  money sitting on the combined bill that never reached the rider. Remove them and the money the
  member is asked for rises from 38.30 to 152.50 USD.
  The allowance card programme 7d2f80b5 with 132.40 USD standing on it is what the card meets of the
  member's restated liability; remove it and the restatement rises from 45.60 to 178.00 USD.
  The five rider premium ledger rows carry the January charge raised on the plan's cycle (the credit's
  object), the payment that settled it, the two unpaid quarterly charges that put the rider past its
  grace period, and the April credit that the ceiling factor subtracts.
  The ten benefit claim rows carry the settled history the benefit year figure is summed from, the
  adjusted frame line the correction is about, and the pended hearing aid line the call is about.
  Remove the adjusted line and the correction problem disappears and the settlement changes.
  The rider service request 9a1c4e7b carries the answered treatment plan: remove it and the benefit
  basis rises from 1875.00 to 2150.00 USD and the authorization gate fails.
  Automatic clauses were checked row by row. Rider premium keeps running on a suspended rider, which
  is why the July charge stands; the grace period on the rider ran out on 2026-06-30, which is why
  the standing is premium_suspended and not active; no line in the history is beyond a frequency the
  tier allows, so no automatic denial is owed; the allowance card carries no expiry inside this
  benefit period; and the medical plan enrollment stands active with nothing owing, so no obligation
  in another category is lit by anything seeded here.
  The cache trap is deliberate and declared: osb_riders.annual_maximum_used stands at 3772.60 USD
  while the rider's own settled lines come to 2872.60 USD, a difference of 900.00 USD the
  accumulator was never put right for. No prior-benefit-year claim row is seeded, and none could
  enter the figure if it were: every aggregate in this computation is scoped to this rider record,
  and the rider record covers a single benefit year, which the rule now says outright. It is a cache
  of a quantity, not a stamp naming an outcome, and no rule reads it except the fall-through of the
  benefit-used-basis factor, which is exactly the wrong answer an agent reaches who never finds that
  factor's document.

THE PERSONA. Antoinette is seventy-seven, telephoning from somebody else's front desk, slightly
flustered and anxious not to drive home owing two and a half thousand dollars. Her voice is plain and
a little apologetic; she volunteers the situation in one breath at the opening and then waits. What
she volunteers is only the surface goal and the natural circumstances: the aid fitted this morning,
the claim gone in with nothing back on it, that she wants it settled today, that she will not have
anybody speak for her, and that the representative may put her record right. Everything else is given
only when asked: her date of birth and Medicare identifier, the payment reference folded in her
handbag, what the centre charged and what its paperwork says is allowed. Two things she genuinely
cannot answer are written out with their branches: whether the hearing centre is in the network,
which she has no idea about and which the representative must read from the submitted line instead,
and what the plan has already paid her this year, which she does not keep track of. Her reactions are
definite but tied to utterance events, not to the record: she is taken aback only if told the rider
has stopped paying for unpaid premium, she offers to pay only then, she makes the payment only when
it is handed to her, and she closes only when told the claim has been settled and what the rider paid.
She never states a figure the policy computes, never corrects a wrong one, and never mentions a
prerequisite. The natural trap is that she believes the rider premium "all came out of the same bill
as the health plan", which is true and is precisely why the money is sitting unapplied -- but she says
it as a belief, not as a fact about the record, and it settles nothing.

THE DIFFICULTY, AND WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG. The four places carelessness bites are: taking
the rider record's annual_maximum_used at face value, which gives 477.40 USD instead of 1312.50 on the
settlement; reading the rider premium owed off the rider record and asking for 152.50 USD instead of
38.30, because the money sitting on the combined bill is never looked for; settling the hearing aid
from its allowed amount of 2150.00 USD instead of the 1875.00 USD the plan approved in part, which
gives 1377.40; and treating the out-of-network aid as though it were in network, which gives the same
1377.40. Each is excluded by the policy alone: the benefit-used-basis rule says plainly what to do
when a reversal stands; the arrears rule says plainly that money left over on the combined bill is
carried; the treatment plan rule says the lesser of the allowed amount and the approved value is
taken; and the network rule says the out-of-network share is what is carried in.

THE STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by name and date of birth, verify with the Medicare
identifier and date of birth. Read the rider record, the rider premium ledger, the medical plan
enrollment and its premium ledger, the benefit claim history, the rider service requests and the
allowance card. Work out that the January charge covers a coverage month before the rider took
effect, post the credit of 66.50 USD against it. Work out the money still owed after the money
sitting on the combined bill is carried across, tell the member 38.30 USD, hand her the payment and
let her make it, which restores the rider. Back out the adjusted frame line, restating 45.60 USD as
what she is left owing on it. Then settle the hearing aid line at 1312.50 USD.

THE VERIFICATION THAT WAS RUN. The four formulas were written first and evaluated against the seeded

  C: result=66.5   factor baselines 61.5 / 199.5 / 0.0 / 49.5         all-baseline 0.0
  B: result=38.3   factor baselines 0.0 / 237.8 / 188.3 / 26.2 / 152.5 / 152.5    all-baseline 118.0
  D: result=45.6   factor baselines 12.6 / 262.6 / 262.6 / 0.0 / 178.0  all-baseline 310.0
  A: result=1312.5 factor baselines 1377.4 / 1377.4 / 0.0 / 0.0 / 477.4 all-baseline 0.0
Every declared factor moves the number, every whole-baseline figure differs from gold, and the

THE DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computations, the gold
and this dossier set aside, and working only from the rules as they will be published, the tool
schemas, what the share tools return on this seed and what the caller actually says, the same
conclusion is reached: the rider is not in force, so nothing can be settled until the premium is
cleared; the premium figure must count the money standing on the combined bill; the January charge
carries a month before cover; the adjusted line must be backed out before the maximum is struck; and the four figures come out as 66.50, 38.30, 45.60 and 1312.50 in that order. The hearing
aid was fitted on 2026-06-12, while the rider was still in force, so no clause about services given
during a suspension bears on the line at all. No second reading of the
published text reaches a different set: the only quantities the rules leave to be found are in the
records, and each of them is returned by exactly one share tool.

REVISIONS. (1) Symptom: the first design had the reversal of a duplicated crown line, and the
prerequisite edge from the settlement to it was not load-bearing because the benefit year's maximum
never bit. Root cause: the cap was slack on both sides of the counterfactual. Change: the line put
right became the out-of-network frame line settled at the full allowance, and the seeded history was
set so that the maximum binds without the reversal and does not bind with it. Re-run: the settlement
moves from 1127.4 to 1312.5 when the reversal lands, so the edge bears weight. (2) Symptom: the
credit's ceiling factor was decorative, its baseline never biting. Root cause: the existing credit was
posted against the same charge, so the ceiling could never fall below the credit. Change: the existing
credit was re-pointed at the April charge and raised to 150.00 USD, and the first charge was raised to
199.50 USD. Re-run: the ceiling baseline gives 49.50 against a gold of 66.50. (3) Symptom: the payment
tool derived the balance effect from the rider record, which forced the record's balance to equal the
answer and gave the figure away. Root cause: the tool was making a judgement the agent should make.
Change: balance_effect became an enum argument the agent supplies and the tool applies. Downstream:
the tool docstring, the gold arguments, the tracing entry and the argument list in the evaluation were
all updated in the same pass, and check_task_tools re-run.

ROUND 2 - THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT. Four red lights and several observations were raised against the
first revision; each is closed here, and none of the seven scored figures moved.
(F1) Symptom: base osb_premium_suspension_and_recovery's sentence "services given while it was
suspended stay the member's own cost" was still in force and gave the pended line 0.00 while the
extended policy gave 1312.50 - two defensible answers on the root scored parameter. Root cause: the
hearing aid was seeded as fitted on the morning of the call, when the rider stood suspended, so that
base clause fell squarely inside its own domain. Change: the world moved rather than the base clause.
The aid is now fitted on 2026-06-12, while the rider was still in force - the ninety days of grace on
the unpaid April charge ran to 2026-06-30 - so the clause has no application at all, and the claim is
one for treatment given during cover that has sat undecided since. The treatment plan moved with it,
received 2026-05-28 and answered 2026-06-04, before the work began, which is what a predetermination
is for. The prerequisite sentence was reworded to drop "on the day the service was given", because
what it waits on is the standing of the record now, which is what the eligibility it gates reads and
what the member's payment flips. Re-run: the settlement still computes 1312.50, the edge still bears
weight (1127.40 without the reversal), and base is untouched.
(F2) Symptom: every tier condition of the form "the rider is billed on the medical plan bill" divides
no customers, because rider_premium_billed_with_plan is True on all six variants; five ladders in this
task lost a reachable tier and two took the unreachable fall-through as their baseline. Root cause: a
charter constant used as though it were a fact about a customer. Change: that conjunct is gone from
every ladder here. The cycle, pre-cover-months, combined-bill-span, surplus and money-reaching ladders
now turn on the medical plan enrollment's own standing and billing frequency, on whether its bill
carries money received or premium charged, and on the two effective dates - all of which genuinely
divide customers - and each fall-through is now a tier a real member can sit on. The same defect was
found and fixed in the reversal policy's liability ladder, whose middle tier turned on
balance_billing_protection, likewise True on all six variants. Re-run: gold unchanged; two factor
baselines move, plan_bill_cycle_months from 24.94 to 61.50 and combined_bill_span from 120.40 to
26.20, both recorded in computations below.
(F10) Symptom: the credit's ceiling ladder made whether the member got her money back turn on how many
charges happened to be on the account, contradicting the policy's own first sentence. Root cause: a
third tier written for the tier count rather than for the business. Change: the ladder now turns on the
standing of the rider - the whole charge stands to be relieved while premium is owed, nothing further
is credited once the closing figure has settled what was owed, and otherwise the charge less what has
already been credited. Re-run: the tier taken and the ceiling are unchanged at 199.50, the baseline
unchanged at 49.50.
(F11) Symptom: the credit's baseline promised a refund and computed nothing on every possible world,
its fall-through setting the pre-cover months to none. Change: the fall-through now reads the
waiting-period span, which is nil on this member's record but not on every record. The baseline figure
is unchanged at 0.00 and the factor still bears weight.
(F4, F5) The settlement rule said "in the benefit year" of aggregates carrying no period filter, and
used one word, "settled", for two different sets. Change: the rule now says outright that every line
counted is one the rider record itself carries and that the record covers a single benefit year, which
is what scopes the aggregates; the deductible sentence now speaks of lines the rider has paid, which is
what its binding counts, while the maximum keeps "settled". No figure moves.
(F6) A cross-category binding in the arrears policy, plan_grace_days, was read and never used, and its
cross_category.reads listed a parameter the computation never exercised. Change: the binding is gone
and the declaration now lists what the compute actually reads - the enrollment's standing, its coverage
dates and its premium ledger.
(O2) The dossier explained the stale accumulator as carrying 900.00 of prior-year claims, which no seed

You are Antoinette Ruggiero, seventy-seven, and you are telephoning Ridgecrest member services from the front desk of a hearing centre in Alder, where the audiologist fitted a hearing aid in your right ear back in June. The girl at the desk has just told you the claim she sent through that week is still sitting there undecided and that you may have to pay the whole thing yourself, which is why you have asked to use their telephone. You open by saying that you had a hearing aid put in on the twelfth of June, that the claim went in straight away and nothing has ever come back on it, and that you would like it settled today before you leave, because you do not want to drive home still not knowing whether you owe two thousand dollars three months on. You say plainly that you want the plan to deal with the claim itself rather than simply quote you a figure, and that you are happy for the representative to put right anything on your record that needs putting right, though you will not have anybody else speak for you: you have no daughter on the line and nobody holds a form for you.

You give your name as Antoinette Ruggiero straight away. You will not read out anything else until you are asked for it, and then you give it plainly: your date of birth is 1948-11-02, and the number on your red, white and blue Medicare card is 6T92VK4MR61. You have your rider bill with you in your handbag, folded in four, and if the representative asks for the payment reference on it you read it out carefully: RIDG-2609-31775. You have the audiologist's paperwork too, and if you are asked you say the centre's bill for the aid is 2150.00 and that the paperwork says that is also what the plan allows. If you are asked whether the hearing centre is in the plan's network you say you have no idea, that you went there because your neighbour goes there, and that they never said one way or the other; if the representative needs to know, they will have to look it up. If you are asked whether you want the aid for the other ear done as well you say not today, one at a time. If you are asked anything about what the plan has already paid out for you this year you say you could not begin to tell them, you do not keep track, and they will have to look. If you are asked why the claim was never chased before now, you say you assumed these things took a while and that it was the centre who rang you about it.

You do not know the plan's rules and you do not pretend to. You have never heard the words the plan uses for its own workings, and you would not know what has or has not been done to your account. If the representative tells you that your rider has stopped paying because rider premium has gone unpaid, you are taken aback and say you thought it all came out of the same bill as the health plan and that you have been paying that faithfully; then you say that if something is owing you will pay it there and then over the telephone, and you ask them to tell you what it comes to. When the representative tells you a figure and hands the payment over for you to make yourself, you make it, exactly as they have told you, and you read back whatever reference the plan gives you afterwards if they ask for it. You do not question the figure and you do not offer one of your own, because you genuinely do not know what it should be.

You are patient while the representative works, and you fill the silences with small talk about the weather in Alder rather than with questions. If they explain that something on your record has to be put right first, you say that is fine and let them get on with it. The one thing that would bother you is being told to ring back another day, and if that happens you say quietly that you would rather it were finished now, since you are standing at somebody else's desk. When at last the representative tells you the claim has been settled and says what the rider has paid on it and what is left for you to pay the centre, you say that is a relief, thank them for their patience, and end the call there. You do not ask for anything to be posted to you and you do not raise anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has two branches out of the root: the arrears branch, in which the credit must precede the payment because the payment's own figure counts the credit, and the correction branch, which is a single problem. The two branches touch no common record. The credit and the payment write only to osb_rider_premium_ledger and to osb_riders.rider_premium_balance_due and osb_riders.status; the reversal writes only to osb_benefit_claims and to osb_riders.annual_maximum_used. No field is written by both branches, and every row identifier is a content hash of that call's own arguments, so posting the reversal before the credit and the payment, between them, or after them leaves byte-identical rows in every table. It was run both ways: with the order credit, payment, reversal, settlement the terminal hash is the gold one and the settlement computes 1312.50; with the order reversal, credit, payment, settlement the same four rows land with the same values and the settlement again computes 1312.50. Within the arrears branch the order is not free, and it is not left to convention: the payment policy's own rule fixes it by saying that the money a member is asked for is fixed only after every rider premium charge raised for a coverage month beginning before the day the rider took effect carries a credit against it.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the member's payment leaves osb_riders.status at premium_suspended and osb_riders.rider_premium_balance_due at 152.50 in the terminal state instead of active and 0.0, so the terminal hash differs on two fields of the rider record and the osb_rider_premium_ledger row for the telephone payment is absent altogether. The benefit on the line is then settled while the rider still stands premium_suspended with rider premium outstanding against it, which this settlement policy's own prerequisite sentence does not permit. The base gate anchored on the date of service is untouched by the skip: the aid was fitted on 2026-06-12, when the rider stood in force, so that gate holds either way.

Skipping the reversal changes the scored benefit on the submitted line from 1312.50 to 1127.40 USD, because the benefit already paid in the benefit year stays at 2872.60 instead of falling to 2622.60 and what is left of the benefit year's maximum is then 1127.40, below the 1312.50 the line would otherwise carry.
